title: Mahlanya Cultural Protocols
description: Schema for Swazi cultural protocols that govern player behaviour and NPC relationship mechanics. Modders can add or modify protocols here without touching C++. Each protocol maps to a UCulturalProtocol data asset in UE5.

protocols.description: Complete list of cultural protocols active in the simulation.

protocol.title: Cultural Protocol
protocol.description: A single named cultural rule. When the player performs the required_actions in the correct context the protocol is Observed; failure or the inverse action marks it Violated. Both outcomes trigger relationship_impact on nearby NPCs.

id.description: Unique protocol identifier. Used as a foreign key in dialogue and quest data. Convention: PROT_<PascalCaseName>.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the protocol shown in the in-game cultural codex. Should contextualise the practice within Swazi history and society.

relationship_impact.description: Delta applied to the player's relationship score with observing NPCs when the protocol is Observed. A negative value here indicates a protocol whose observation still carries a cost (rare). Violation always applies the negation of this value.

status_on_observe.description: The protocol status flag set when the player correctly performs all required_actions. Always 'Observed' — kept as an enum for future extensibility.

status_on_violate.description: The protocol status flag set when the player fails or inverts the required behaviour. Always 'Violated' — kept as an enum for future extensibility.

required_actions.description: Ordered list of player actions that must be performed to satisfy the protocol. Actions are symbolic strings parsed by the protocol evaluation subsystem. Examples: 'crouch', 'clap_twice', 'say_sawubona', 'remove_hat', 'offer_snuff'.

examples.description: Swazi custom requires greeting an elder by crouching slightly, clapping twice with cupped hands and saying 'Sawubona' (I see you). Failure to do so is a serious mark of disrespect that damages relations with the elder's clan.

Entering the royal cattle kraal without permission and without removing headwear is a grave insult to the Ingwenyama. Visitors must await acknowledgement at the gate, remove any hat or head covering, and avert their gaze until addressed.
